name: FL-23
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about nine points on the partisan baseline
Frankel is a well-funded incumbent with $1.2M on hand versus under $40K for Adeimy
Prediction markets price Democratic win chances around 95%
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Frankel: a +9 Democratic district, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage over a lightly funded challenger. Markets at 95% for Democrats corroborate a safe seat, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-implied margin of about 20 points.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Frankel or a strong Republican fundraising push could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lois Frankel seeks another term in a South Florida district that voted about nine points Democratic at the presidential level. She enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised $2.3 million and holding $1.2 million on hand, while Republican challenger Deborah Adeimy has raised about $163,000 with modest cash remaining. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race.

With no public general-election polling available, the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and the funding gap, all of which favor Frankel. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price her win probability around 95%, consistent with a safe Democratic seat.
